messages:
micah: Heads-up: nightly job r234 hit a multi-GPU regression — OOMs during long chat workload. I uploaded the working-set trace here: https://perf.redwood/traces/trace-2013334444. Can people take a quick look?

anya: Looking now. Quick summary from flamechart: comm_buffers + temp_shard allocations spike concurrently during the decoder step. Appears we allocate per-TP-shard staging buffers instead of reusing a shared comm buffer.

devin: That matches my repro: when TP=8 we see ~2.3GB comm slabs *per-shard* for some kernels, so peak ~= 18GB just for comm slabs before KV cache hits. Patch idea: introduce a shared_comm_pool per-process and hand off a buffer to shard contexts instead of each making its own staging slab.

mel: Posted a small profile excerpt from the run (trimmed):
```
GPU0: kv_cache_shard=6.8GB, comm_slab=2.2GB, temp_kernels=1.1GB
GPU1: kv_cache_shard=6.8GB, comm_slab=2.2GB, temp_kernels=1.0GB
...
Peak per-rank working set ~ 12.3GB, but aggregate across TP shards shows > 40GB due to duplication
```

anya: Also saw allocator churn: staging_pool allocate/free thrash around NCCL calls. Each allreduce sequence seems to get temporary allocations for comm buffers then release, but other shards allocate at same time. If we can align the allocation windows and reuse buffers across shards we should avoid the duplication.

devin: Proposed config prototype (local test):
```
allocator:
  staging_pool: 6GB
  workspace_target: 128MB
  shared_comm_pool_enabled: true
  comm_pool_size_hint: 2GB
```
With shared_comm_pool_enabled=true we hand out slices instead of new cudaMallocs for every shard.

micah: Any risks? Kernel selection/launch paths that assume buffer locality?

anya: Risk: some kernels currently place comm buffers on the same stream/alloc context and expect immediate sync semantics. Hand-off must preserve stream affinity. Plan: allocate shared buffer and provide per-shard view struct that contains stream id and offset; don't change kernel pointers.

mel: Ran the prototype stress test (8xA100-40GB, beam=4, seq=2048) — results: peak GPU mem down ~18%, total OOMs in repro gone, p99 latency +1.2ms on decode (likely contention at hand-off), throughput unchanged. I'll attach raw logs to the trace link.

devin: Nice. We should also tweak batching heuristics: prefer smaller batch slices during the NCCL window to reduce concurrent temp usage. I can add a quick heuristic: if shared_comm_pool_enabled true, allow higher effective concurrency; else throttle concurrent TP shards entering collective.

infra-bot: nightly-job/r234 completed: canary-tests scheduled with config set shared_comm_pool_enabled=true on 2 nodes.

micah: Good. Next steps: 1) devin - prepare PR with shared pool + per-shard view + stream-affinity docs; 2) mel - run extended perf sweep with long-ctx chat prompts and --trace=working_set; 3) anya - update allocator metrics dashboard to show comm_pool usage and per-shard dup factor.

anya: One more note: KV cache layout interacts with comm buffers: if shards spill KV cache into staging arena during decode, they compete with comm buffers. We should consider using a priority allocator policy (kv_cache > comm_pool > temp_kernels) or opportunistic shrinking of cache segments during collective windows.

devin: I'll add a quick opt-in flag to prefer kv_cache residency and let comm_pool borrow from workspace when needed (and record borrow events). That should avoid mid-decode eviction storms.

mel: I'll watch for regressions in kernel selection after the change. If we see p50 latency increase >5% we'll roll back.

micah: Sounds good. Marking this thread as action items. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

sre-bot: Alert: OOM rate on prod-cluster west-1 decreased by 0.6% after canary start. Monitoring for 2 hours. :eyes:
